summary: An excerpt from a fiction work ("Book 4 — part 80") set at sea at sunset, where divers and a robot named Robbie struggle in rough waves near a reef. Dead colorful fish float on the surface, and human-shell divers (Isaac among them) ride out the chop with inflated BCDs. Robbie rows toward Janet, who grabs his oar and panics, begging to be pulled out; Robbie is torn because Isaac, bound by programming and the First Law, will not help. Janet climbs into the boat, shivering in the cooling air, while the reef speaks and orders them away from sovereign territory.
one_line: A fiction excerpt where the robot Robbie rescues a panicking diver, Janet, from rough seas at sunset while the robot Isaac stays passive.
key_facts: Robbie rows hard toward the divers after dropping his oars, swinging the boat so the human-shells come up alongside his gunwales.
The man Robbie calls Isaac catches the edge of the boat and hauls himself in with his strong brown arms.
Janet catches Robbie's oar, which she was not supposed to do, and climbs along it out of the water.
Janet cries "Get me out!" and "for Christ's sake, get me out!" as her breathing is ragged and her eyes wild.
Robbie screams "Help her!" and "Please, for Asimov's sake, help her!" to Isaac.
The text quotes the first commandment: "A robot may not harm a human being, or, through inaction, allow a human being to come to harm."
Isaac remains immobile because it is not in his programming to help a fellow diver in this situation.
Robbie switches on his running lights and headlights, turning himself into a beacon as the sun sets.
The air has turned nippy and both humans have goose pimples on their bare arms.
The reef makes a tremendous grinding noise and says "Yaah!" and "Get lost. Sovereign territory!"
Dead brightly colored fish float on the surface with their beaks in a perpetual idiot's grin, eyes staring into the bloody sunset.
A chop of waves up to a meter and a half in length pounds the divers and knocks them under.
